prospective

pruh-SPEK-tiv (stress on SPEK) · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Expected to become something or to happen, though it has not yet.

The prospective student toured the campus twice before sending in her application.

Example

The team scheduled open tryouts to give every prospective player a fair chance to show her skills.

Prospective tells you these players might join the team but have not joined it. The word looks forward at what a person may become, while promising nothing about it.

How prospective sits among its neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

future

future: coming later and sure to arrive

possible

possible: able to happen, though it may not

Antonyms

former

former: having been something before, but no longer

current

current: happening or holding a place right now

How Strong Is It? — possible → prospective → certain

possible vs. prospective

possible vs. prospective: Possible is weaker than prospective: possible only means something could happen, while prospective means a person or plan is actually expected, with steps already pointing that way.

certain vs. prospective

certain vs. prospective: Certain is stronger than prospective: a prospective event is expected but could still fall through, while a certain one will definitely happen no matter what.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — pro

prefix — pro: forward

root — spect

root — spect: to look

suffix — ive

suffix — ive: having the quality of

Put it together

Put it together: Stack pro- ('forward') on spect ('to look') and cap it with -ive ('having the quality of'): prospective means 'forward-looking' - describing someone or something being looked at for what it may soon become.

Use the root in a new word: inspect

Use the root in a new word: inspect: Prospective and inspect both carry the Latin root spect, 'to look.' The referee stopped to inspect the ball before restarting the game, turning it over in her hands while the players waited.

Root Check

Word Choice

Prospective sits before nouns about people and plans: prospective buyer, prospective student, prospective member. It is the careful word for 'may become,' promising nothing. Take care not to swap it with 'perspective,' which sounds close but means a point of view.
